You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual ARC: rectangular zero patch

## Trigger
A large structured grid contains a contiguous rectangular region of `0`s, while the requested output is a smaller grid with the same dimensions as that zero region.

## Approach
1. Locate the exact bounding box of the zero rectangle; do not assume it is centered or square.
2. Check whether the output should reconstruct the hidden contents by comparing analogous positions in repeated, mirrored, or periodically repeated parts of the surrounding design.
3. Test candidate transformations (direct repetition, horizontal/vertical reflection, 180-degree rotation, and repeated tile offsets) against the visible cells and any demonstrations. Use the demo output to determine orientation and offset.
4. Submit only the reconstructed rectangle, preserving row/column orientation and exact dimensions. Do not include the surrounding grid.
5. If demonstrations are available, request one when the mapping/orientation is genuinely ambiguous; each request and wrong submission has a cost, so prefer deductions supported by visible repetition.

## Evidence and caution
A solved Continual-ARC instance had a 24x24 patterned grid with a 3x3 zero patch and the correct output was a 3x3 grid. A demonstration from the same task family showed an 8x5 zero patch paired with an 8x5 output. This supports matching output dimensions to the blank rectangle and recovering its contents, but does not establish one universal symmetry rule. Verify the specific alignment from each instance rather than blindly copying a guessed transform.
